name: alf_crb
label: alpha CrB (Alphecca, A0 V + G5 V detached eclipsing binary, P = 17.36 d; the A0 V primary alone)
sources: Tomkin & Popper 1986, AJ 91, 1428: R_A 2.89-3.04 Rsun, R_B 0.90 Rsun, M_A 2.58, M_B 0.92 Msun, P 17.3599 d, e 0.37; total eclipse of the G5 V secondary
van Leeuwen 2007: parallax 43.46 +/- 0.28 mas (23.0 pc); Gaia DR3 42.24 +/- 0.98 mas
notes: theta 1.21 mas = 2 x 3.0 Rsun / 23.0 pc (from the eclipse radius and the Hipparcos parallax, not measured; the 1986 radius is uncertain by 2-3 %). The G5 V secondary contributes < 1 % of the blue light and is ignored; the pair is 3-6 mas apart, inside any pupil field.
Science: a 0.3 % blue diameter plus a modern (TESS) eclipse radius gives a geometric distance for a star whose Gaia parallax is 2.3 %; Hipparcos is 0.6 %.
